headline: AGENTS.md Standardizes AI Agent Context Files
summary: The open-source AGENTS.md standard aims to unify context files for coding agents, reducing maintenance headaches and ensuring consistent behavior across tools.
details: Developers often face a confusing array of context files like AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and others, leading to duplicated effort and potential inconsistencies. The AGENTS.md standard, now under the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, proposes a single Markdown file to serve as the source of truth for coding agents.

This initiative, backed by major players like OpenAI and Google, has seen adoption in over 60,000 open-source repositories and supports more than 28 tools. The core idea is to eliminate the need for developers to manually sync multiple context files that quickly drift out of sync.

While AGENTS.md is gaining traction, it's important to note that support for specific tools, like Claude Code, remains unconfirmed by official Anthropic documentation. Developers relying on Claude Code are advised to keep CLAUDE.md as a fallback until native AGENTS.md support is officially verified.

The standard supports a cascading structure, similar to .gitignore or .eslintrc, where the nearest AGENTS.md file takes precedence. This allows for context to be defined at the root level for general project-wide settings and overridden within specific packages for tailored configurations.

For seamless migration, developers can rename their existing context files to AGENTS.md and create a symbolic link (symlink) from the old filename to the new one. This ensures that legacy tools continue to function while new tools leverage the unified standard, preventing duplicate maintenance.

Effective AGENTS.md files should be operational rather than aspirational, focusing on commands the agent can execute verbatim, project-specific conventions not inferable from code, and avoiding explanations already present in package.json or folder structures. An AGENTS.md file longer than the README likely contains redundant information.

headline: Nvidia Nemotron 3.5 Lightning: 4x Faster AI Agent Output for Smarter Systems
summary: Nvidia unveils Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B-parameter model designed for high-efficiency, long-running agentic AI workloads, boasting up to 4x faster output speeds.
details: Nvidia is expanding its Nemotron 3 model family with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, the highest-efficiency model in its class for long-running agentic AI workloads. This release follows Nemotron 3 Nano and reflects Nvidia’s commitment to continually improving open models for greater accuracy and speed.

Built for specialized tasks within larger multi-agent systems, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, helps create smarter and more efficient agentic applications. Nvidia is also releasing NeMo Switchyard, an open-source library for smart routing inside popular agent tools, allowing enterprises to build routers based on their specific needs.

Together, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Switchyard deliver greater control over how AI is deployed, where it runs and how efficiently it operates across PCs, workstations, data centers and the cloud. Modern agentic systems increasingly operate as systems of models, or model ensembles, with different models specialized for different tasks.

Nvidia Nemotron open models are designed for this architecture. A frontier reasoning model may plan and orchestrate a workflow, while smaller specialized models like Nemotron 3.5 Lightning can perform targeted tasks such as code review, tool use, security alert monitoring and answering billing questions.

Nemotron 3.5 Lightning delivers up to 4x faster output speed, leading to 30% faster agentic task completion compared with other models in its class. Because it’s open and customizable, it can be easily post-trained with Nvidia NeMo on an organization’s own domain data, tools and workflows to improve accuracy for specialized tasks.

AI leaders across industries are customizing Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for their workloads, including CrowdStrike for cybersecurity, Harvey with Trajectory for legal services and CodeRabbit with Baseten for code review. Lila Sciences is helping to improve reasoning capabilities for agentic tasks across physical and life sciences, and Fastino Labs customized the model for leading accuracies in software development, finance and healthcare workloads.

Nemotron 3.5 Lightning also gives organizations control over privacy and deployment. It can run on local AI systems, including Nvidia RTX PCs, Nvidia DGX Spark, Nvidia DGX Station and Nvidia Jetson, or scale across edge AI devices, Nvidia RTX PRO workstations, data centers and cloud environments for enterprise use cases.

Nvidia NeMo Switchyard is an open-source model routing library for AI agents. The technology routes prompts to the most capable and efficient model for each step of an agent workflow automatically, based on specific needs. Agent application developers can tune or modify the router with different routing algorithms to optimize performance.
